topics.name: Security Incident Response Overview and Data Visualization
topics.description: Understand the Security Incident Response application architecture, data visualization capabilities, and how SIR fits within Security Operations.

introduction.overview: Security Incident Response (SIR) provides a structured approach to handling security incidents from detection through resolution. It integrates with threat intelligence and other security tools to provide context-rich incident management.
introduction.whyItMatters: Overview and Data Visualization covers 15% of the CIS-SIR exam. This foundational knowledge is essential for understanding how all other SIR components work together.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master the SIR data model, understand security incident states and workflows, and know how dashboards visualize security posture. Be familiar with the Security Operations suite components.
introduction.examTips: Know the relationship between security incidents, observables, and threat intelligence. Understand the incident lifecycle and how visualization tools help security analysts.

topics.name: Security Incident Creation and Threat Intelligence
topics.description: Learn how security incidents are created, classified, and enriched with threat intelligence data.

introduction.overview: Security incidents can be created manually, through integrations, or via automated detection. Threat intelligence enriches these incidents with context about known threats, attack patterns, and indicators of compromise.
introduction.whyItMatters: Incident Creation and Threat Intelligence accounts for 14% of the CIS-SIR exam. Understanding how incidents are identified and enriched is foundational to effective response.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know the different incident creation methods, understand threat intelligence sources and feeds, and learn how observables are extracted and matched against intelligence.
introduction.examTips: Focus on the relationship between threat intelligence and incident enrichment. Know how STIX/TAXII feeds work and how indicators of compromise are matched.

topics.name: Security Incident and Threat Intelligence Integrations
topics.description: Configure integrations with SIEM, SOAR, and threat intelligence platforms to enhance security incident response capabilities.

introduction.overview: SIR's power comes from its integrations with security tools across the enterprise. These include SIEM platforms, endpoint detection tools, threat intelligence providers, and orchestration systems.
introduction.whyItMatters: Integrations cover 14% of the CIS-SIR exam. This tests your knowledge of connecting SIR to the broader security ecosystem.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand common SIEM integrations (Splunk, QRadar), know how to configure threat intelligence feeds, and learn about orchestration integrations for automated response.
introduction.examTips: Know the major integration patterns and what data flows between systems. Understand the difference between pull-based and push-based integrations.

topics.name: Security Incident Response Management
topics.description: Master the tools and processes for managing security incidents through investigation, containment, and resolution.

introduction.overview: Effective incident management requires structured processes for investigation, containment, eradication, and recovery. SIR provides workflows and tools to guide analysts through each phase.
introduction.whyItMatters: Incident Management represents 15% of the CIS-SIR exam. Questions focus on practical incident handling scenarios and workflow configuration.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know the incident response phases, understand how to use the analyst workspace, and learn about task assignment and collaboration features.
introduction.examTips: Focus on the incident response lifecycle (NIST framework). Know how tasks are created and assigned during incident response and how to document findings.

topics.name: Automation and Standard Processes
topics.description: Configure playbooks, automated responses, and standard operating procedures to accelerate incident response.

introduction.overview: Automation is critical for handling the volume and speed of security threats. SIR supports playbooks, automated actions, and integration with orchestration tools.
introduction.whyItMatters: Automation is the largest domain at 30% of the CIS-SIR exam. This reflects the importance of automated response in modern security operations.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master playbook creation and execution, understand automated enrichment and response actions, and know how to integrate with SOAR platforms.
introduction.examTips: Focus heavily on playbooks - how they're structured, triggered, and executed. Know common automation use cases like IP blocking, user disabling, and ticket creation.

topics.name: Risk Calculations and Post Incident Response
topics.description: Understand how security risks are calculated, reported, and how post-incident activities improve future response.

introduction.overview: Risk calculation helps prioritize incidents and resources. Post-incident activities like lessons learned and metrics analysis drive continuous improvement.
introduction.whyItMatters: Risk and Post-Incident covers 12% of the CIS-SIR exam. This tests understanding of how incidents impact organizational risk and how to improve over time.
introduction.keyConcepts: Know how incident severity and impact are calculated, understand risk scoring, and learn about post-incident review processes and reporting.
introduction.examTips: Focus on risk calculation factors and how they influence prioritization. Know the components of a post-incident review and what metrics matter.
